interface.signature: logistic_map(width: int, height: int, x_coords: list[int], y_coords: list[int]) -> list[list[int | None]]

preconditions.description: The map dimensions must be positive integers.
The number of x coordinates must equal the number of y coordinates.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < width for x in x_coords) and all(0 <= y < height for y in y_coords)
preconditions.description: All supply points must lie within the map boundaries.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == height and all(len(row) == width for row in return_value)
postconditions.description: The output must be a 2D list with dimensions matching the input width and height.

postconditions.expression: all(x_coords and y_coords or all(cell is None for row in return_value for cell in row))
postconditions.description: If there are no supply points, every cell in the output must be None. Otherwise, every cell must contain the Manhattan distance to the closest supply point.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < height and 0 <= j < width for i in range(height) for j in range(width) if return_value[i][j] is not None)
postconditions.description: For each cell (i, j) with a supply point, the distance must be a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i][j] == min(abs(i - y) + abs(j - x) for x, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords)) if x_coords and y_coords else None for i in range(height) for j in range(width))
postconditions.description: Each cell's value must be the minimum Manhattan distance to any supply point, or None if no supply points exist.
